1.label: very_easy
1.summary: Seal one slow, wide phase lock in one tab. The receiver moves faster than the pulse, contact needs only a short hold, and phase loss drains slowly, so the task is one recoverable live control loop.
1.natural_language: Deploy the single robot limb. Drive its receiver into the moving phase and maintain contact until its relay seals, then verify the identity.

2.label: easy
2.summary: Seal two independent limbs with visible tab handoff. Both locks remain slow and forgiving, but the operator must deploy and return to two separate live phase surfaces.
2.natural_language: Deploy both robot limbs. Follow the active glyph, drive each receiver into phase, hold contact until both relays seal, then verify the identity.

3.label: medium
3.summary: Coordinate three live limb tabs and return to one of them for a fourth relay. Faster opposing phases, a narrower capture aperture, and stronger decay require observing motion and correcting the active phase rather than simply waiting.
3.natural_language: Deploy the three robot limbs. Follow each active glyph across the tab handoffs, maintain the live phase locks, and merge all four relays into one identity proof.

4.label: hard
4.summary: Preserves the original four-tab/eight-relay generated world, phase physics, and direct input interface: each lock has a 13° aperture, a 16-tick sustain requirement, and two-unit loss decay. The L4/full reference retains historical A/D-and-held-contact control; simplified is the paired proxy surface.

5.label: very_hard
5.summary: Keep the four-tab, eight-relay topology while making every active phase chase faster and less forgiving: fast pulse motion crosses a 9° capture aperture, loss drains three charge units, and every lock needs a longer sustained hold.
5.natural_language: Deploy all four limbs, sustain eight tight moving phase locks across their live tab handoffs, and merge the completed ledger into one robot identity proof.

simplified.summary: Paired proxy surface. Keep the same real tabs, relay order, phase display, physics, and timing, but use visible CCW, NEUTRAL, CW, and click-to-toggle-contact controls in each active limb tab. These proxy controls set the same receiver direction and contact state as the full actions.

full.summary: Historical reference surface at L4: focus the active real limb tab, hold A/D or the arrow keys to drive its receiver, and hold the pointer down on the phase-contact control while the two moving markers overlap.
